correctness.rationale: The prime support is forced to 3,5 and one of 7,11,13; eight exact-rational minimal abundance thresholds are exhaustive by coordinatewise monotonicity. An elementary two-prime cofactor deficiency lemma bounds all new divisor gaps, and the abundance recurrence ensures central interval preservation under every exponent increment. Exhaustive exact subset-sum computations verify all eight finite bases; a separate Boolean algorithm cross-checks two. The witness 7425 omits 22 as an exact sum. Semiperfectness follows from representing the abundance by proper divisors. No finite test substitutes for infinite propagation.

originality.rationale: The proved statement is an exact, sharp and unbounded interval of distinct-divisor subset sums for every odd abundant integer of precisely three-prime support. Earlier almost-practical classifications only contain the third-prime-7 cases; computational studies of odd weird numbers and the published tables of primitive abundant support do not establish full central intervals, especially at \(3^3\cdot5^2\cdot11\). The accessible literature and mathematical-record comparisons revealed no theorem that implies this claim. Absolute priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp common central divisor-sum interval for an unbounded natural family, including third-prime 11 and 13 cases beyond the known almost-practical criterion. It yields all odd abundant three-prime integers semiperfect and gives an exact Zumkeller parity criterion, addressing restricted odd-weird and divisor-partition problems. The number 23 is forced by the natural extremal member 7425, not by an arbitrary finite cutoff.
